source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 1, 9. Δῆλον δὲ ὅτι ἡ μὲν ὑγιαίνουσα ψυχὴ ἢ κἂν τοιαύτη γε εἶναι βουλομένη ταῦτα πράττει, οὐ τοσοῦτον τὸ παρὸν μόνον σκοποῦσα, ὅσον προορωμένη τί καὶ εἰς τὰ μέλλοντα ἐκ τῶν ἐπιτελουμένων ἀπαντηθήσεται. καὶ ἐὰν μὲν χρηστοῦ τινος νομιζομένου ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος γίνεσθαι προθεωρῇ τὸ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι πικρόν, παραπεμψαμένη τὸ δοκοῦν εἶναι ἡδὺ τὸ ἐναντίον πράττει, ὑπὲρ τοῦ μὴ μετὰ ταῦτα χαλεπῷ τινι περιπεσεῖν· ἐὰν δὲ ἐπιπόνου τυγχάνοντος τοῦ παρόντος ἀγαθαὶ ἐλπίδες διαδέχωνται τὸ φαινόμενον σκληρόν, ἑκου. σίως αὑτὴν ἐπιδώσει τῇ τραχύτητι τοῦ δόξαντος ἃν εἶναι δεινοῦ παρά τισιν, ἐπὶ τῷ τυχεῖν τῶν διὰ τὸ ὑπομεμενηκέναι ταῦτα διαδεχομένων γλυκέων τὰ σκληρά.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] And it is clear that the healthy soul—or at least the one wanting to be such—does these things, not looking so much at the present alone as foreseeing what also unto the future will meet from the things being accomplished. And if, something thought useful coming to be for the present, she foresees the bitterness in the future, dismissing what seems to be sweet she does the opposite, for the sake of not later falling into something hard; and if, the present being toilsome, good hopes succeed what appears harsh, she will voluntarily give herself over to the roughness of what would seem terrible to some, for the sake of attaining the sweet things that succeed the harsh ones because of having endured these.
pass_b_english: And it is clear that the healthy soul—or at least the one wanting to be such—does these things, not looking so much at the present alone as foreseeing what also unto the future will meet from the things being accomplished. And if, something thought useful coming to be for the present, she foresees the bitterness in the future, dismissing what seems to be sweet she does the opposite, for the sake of not later falling into something hard; and if, the present being toilsome, good hopes succeed what appears harsh, she will voluntarily give herself over to the roughness of what would seem terrible to some, for the sake of attaining the sweet things that succeed the harsh ones because of having endured these (Lamentations 1:9).

choices.why: Origen’s image of the fallen soul as storm-tossed in Lam 1:8 commentary.
